a2-unit-16.16.1 Article:
Reporter: Fashion forward. Can fashion be green?
Reporter: If you follow fashion, you know that nothing stays the same for long. Short skirts are in one season and out the next. You buy a must-have red coat, and a few months later, everybody is wearing blue. And what happens to the clothes that you don't want anymore? Many of them go in the trash. According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Americans produced about seventeen million tons of textile waste in twenty eighteen, and about two thirds of it went to landfills.
Reporter: Grace Kim is a young designer who wants to change this. She has a small studio in Chicago where she makes jackets and bags out of old jeans. Denim is a material that lasts for years, she says. The jeans that people throw away are perfect for new clothes.
Reporter: Grace also works with older women who know how to knit and sew. On Saturdays, they teach crafts to young people at the studio. Sewing is a skill that everybody can learn, says Grace. And the clothes you make yourself are always special.
Reporter: Thrift stores are another part of the answer. These are stores where you can buy second-hand clothes for very little money. Many young Americans love them because they can find clothes that nobody else has.
Reporter: Of course, one designer can't change the whole fashion industry. But we can all buy fewer clothes, choose materials which don't damage the environment, and give away the clothes we don't wear. Fashion can be beautiful and green at the same time.
